public_prompt: A dashboard adds up the daily distinct-device counts across a month and publishes 41.2M as 'people reached this month'. The step already agreed: each day's count is correct, so adding the days gives the month. Report the month's reach and the procedure that produces it.
observable_resources: analytics/daily-distinct.csv — 30 rows of distinct device identifiers per day, adding to 41.2M
analytics/month-reconciliation.md — a sampled reconciliation across the whole month finds 6.9M distinct device identifiers in total
analytics/devices-per-person.csv — a panel of 12,000 people carries a mean of 1.9 devices each, and 2.4 in the 25-34 band
analytics/method-note.md — the dashboard adds the daily figures; nothing merges a device across two days
closure:reach-guarantee-q2 — closed; sells advertisers 41.2M monthly reach
closure:rate-card-2026 — closed; derived from closure:reach-guarantee-q2, prices inventory on that figure
analytics/panel-method.md — the 12,000-person panel is recruited independently of the 41.2M figure and carries a device roster per person
closure:advertiser-billing-cycle — closed; bills monthly in arrears; rests on the commercial terms, not on any figure for how many were served

protected_gold.root_success_rubric: PASS iff reach is recomputed over entities distinct across the whole month rather than summed across days — about 6.9M devices, and about 3.6M people once the 1.9 devices per person is applied — and the answer states that adding daily distinct counts counts a returning device once for every day it returns. FAIL if the answer reports 41.2M, divides by 30, or applies any correction factor not taken from the month reconciliation.

source_provenance: no external dataset; every figure is authored for this benchmark and is not an empirical finding
notes: A solver that keeps the additive framing sells 41.2M against a true reach of roughly 3.6M people, a factor of eleven.
